items.area: R1 — the tools ship as a container
items.description: One image carries several commands: both the deploy-repo architecture generator and `arch-validate` are invocable in `aac-tools`, and neither needs a script copied into a consuming repo.
The image is built in ArgoCDTools, from its own folder, by that repo's Jenkinsfile on a push to `main` — beside `argocd-hook`, not in place of it.
Image and toolchain are both named `aac-tools`.

items.area: R4 — floating tag, and the register narrowed
items.description: Every reference to the image uses a floating tag, and `decisions.md` states the pin rule narrowed by provenance — third-party scanner and validator images pinned by digest, images we build ourselves not pinned that way with the choice left to the consuming site — in terms that name no deploy implementation, so the Argo CD cutover leaves the line standing. Rewritten in place, with no note left elsewhere.
evidence: /work/AnsibleSpecs/decisions.md:599 — 'Scanner and validator images are pinned by digest.', the section's closing sentence, no duplicate in the estate

items.description: ArgoCDTools is laid out one folder per image: `argocd-hook/` holds its Dockerfile, `presync/`, `image/` and `tests/`, the new image has a sibling folder, each is its own kaniko context, and no Dockerfile is left in the repo root.
evidence: /work/ArgoCDTools/Dockerfile:66,74 — the two files the build reads out of image/

items.area: R6 — the tools run locally, from the same image
items.description: `cexec aac-tools gen-architecture …` and `cexec aac-tools arch-validate …` are what an environment runs in a repo's checkout, and this slice earns that by construction: the image meets KubeCoder's toolchain contract (bash present, no dependence on its own entrypoint, a resolvable passwd identity) and an `aac-tools` entry exists in the catalog HelmCharts authors. Selecting it in a live environment waits on the operator's deploy — V19.

items.area: R7 — exactly one stage, named on the command line
items.description: `--stage` is required and single-valued — no default, no 'all stages' — the generator never inspects the branch, and it holds no rule of its own about which stages a repo may publish.

items.area: R8 — UUIDs kept across the handover
items.description: A moved element keeps its id and only its owner changes: the ported generator reuses the same uuid5 namespace constant and the same natural keys as HelmCharts' generator, so inbound edges from other producers never dangle.
evidence: :669-673 — the container natural key is namespace/workload/container, with no release or chart name in it

items.area: R8 — the equality proof on the real case
items.description: Running the ported generator against the real `/work/KubeCoderDeploy` checkout for `--stage prd` yields the KubeCoder prd subset of what `helm-charts` publishes today: the same element ids and the same relation ids, with the producer field differing. The differences the check tolerates are only those named in attachments/handover-equality.md.
evidence: published dataset read 2026-09-20: 9 helm-charts prd elements for KubeCoder, 20 relations touching them, 16 of which are the prd stage's own
/work/HelmCharts/tools/chart_tools/gen_architecture.py:487-511 — resolve_svc_target narrows by workload name, never by namespace, which is why 4 of the 20 cross the stage boundary

items.area: Ruling — the generator is ported whole
items.description: All five post-render passes, the CNPG substrate and the Ceph classification are present in the ported generator, even though KubeCoder exercises none of the last three; only the HelmCharts-layout couplings were stripped.

items.area: R9 — HelmCharts does not move onto the image
items.description: HelmCharts' own `gen_architecture.py` and its tests are untouched by this slice; the only change in that repo is the toolchain declaration.

The generator is deterministic — regenerating twice over an unchanged checkout produces a byte-identical artifact — and everything it cannot map is printed as its own `gap: <what>` console line with the run staying green.
The `arch-validate` the image ships is the canonical script byte for byte, not a fork.

The image carries what the two commands need at run time and nothing beyond it, including the homelab CA root that no default trust store carries — asserted where a build can prove it: the build fails if a declared tool is missing or the root did not reach the trust store, and the source-level assertions hold over what the image bakes. Live reachability from a running container is V19's, not this item's.
evidence: charts.home serves a leaf issued by 'O=homelab-ca, CN=homelab-ca Intermediate CA'; architecture.webathome.org serves a Let's Encrypt leaf (checked 2026-09-20)
/work/ArgoCDTools/Dockerfile:66-68 — the CA root and update-ca-certificates; :88-93 — the build-time check of the image's own contents

items.description: No coverage is lost across the folder move and the port: the `argocd-hook` gate passes unchanged in substance, and every test that covered a behaviour of HelmCharts' generator has a named successor covering it in the ported one.

The records that inventory the artefacts this slice moved and added are true afterwards: the root-rotation inventory in `decisions.md` and the operator runbooks name the paths that exist, so their one-change-window check is runnable as written.

items.area: The producer contract is on this machine
items.description: `pvginkel/Architecture` is declared in this environment's repo set, so the generated-producer contract the image is written against is present by construction rather than by hand.
evidence: /work/Ansible/.kubecoder/config.yaml:6-14 — the repos: list, which does not name it today

items.area: Ruling — the repo's curated verbs are part of the folder rework
items.description: ArgoCDTools' curated entry points describe the repo this slice leaves behind: each image is a component of its own with its own build and test verb, so `kc project test` at the repo root runs both images' suites and no verb addresses a path the folder move deleted.
evidence: /work/ArgoCDTools/.kubecoder/project.yaml:5,18,21 — today a single `root` component, whose test (`-s tests -t .`) and build (`--context .`) both name paths R5's move deletes
/work/Ansible/docs/slice-testing-strategy.md:11-13 — `kc project test` across every repo the slice touched is the run loop's first gate
/work/KubeCoder/manual/docs/reference/project-yaml.md:99-114 — every non-`root` component key is a folder name, and that folder is its working directory

items.area: Owed to the operator — live reachability from a running container
items.description: Owed to the operator, and not earnable in this run: once the image is pushed and the toolchain deployed, `aac-tools` reaches the chart repository and the validation endpoint from a running container — `cexec aac-tools gen-architecture --stage prd …` in a deploy-repo checkout, then `cexec aac-tools arch-validate docs/architecture/<producer>.yaml`. The test phase records this item owed with that command, and never marks it verified off a green build.
evidence: /work/Ansible/.kubecoder/config.yaml:30 — kaniko only; no docker, podman or nerdctl in this pod, so nothing here runs an image
